title: CHAPTER THIRTY-NINE. On the permission of sin, its foundation, opposite, connections, and consequences
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): that same which cannot be out from God who stands as most highly good — they denied Gods providence itself — ignorance belonging toward this doctrine makes it that same when some could not understand whence sin stands as — inasmuch as it stands as ye highest evil that same stands as given. Arminius also attempted it more than once. This locus on permission ye most learned Twisse inquired into; that same which stands as an act belonging toward divine providence concerning it, by means belonging toward that same which all impediments that same God knows would, if applied to ye humans power or will, really impede ye sin, plus also compelling forces that same efficaciously drive toward doing what one abhors, stand as suspended — next follows its PERMISSION. Thus far concerning sin: plus its foundation, opposite, connections, plus consequences — on ye permission belonging toward sin. CHAPTER THIRTY-NINE.
pass_b_english: CHAPTER THIRTY-NINE. On the permission of sin, and its foundation, opposite, connections, and consequences.

Thus far concerning sin: next follows its PERMISSION, which is an act of divine providence concerning it, by which all impediments that God knows would, if applied to the humans power or will, really impede the sin, and also compelling forces that efficaciously drive toward doing what one abhors, are suspended. This locus on permission the most learned Twisse inquired into; Arminius also attempted it more than once. Ignorance of this doctrine makes it that when some could not understand whence sin is — inasmuch as it is the highest evil that is given, which cannot be from God who is most highly good — they denied Gods providence itself.
source_text: CAPUT TRIGESIMUM NONUM, De permissione peccati, eiusque fundamento, opposito, connexis et consequentibus. HActenus de peccato: sequitur eius PERMISSIO, quae est actus divinae providentiae circa illud, quo omnia impedimenta quae Deus novit, si adhiberentur potentiae aut voluntati hominis, peccatum reipsa impeditura, tum cogentia quae efficaciter impellunt ad agendum a quo quis abhorret, suspenduntur. Locum hunc de permissione inquisivit doctissimus Twissus; Arminius quoque non semel tentavit. Ignoratio huius doctrinae efficit ut cum quidam intelligere non possent unde peccatum sit, utpote summum malum quod datur, quod a Deo summe bono esse nequit, ipsam Dei providentiam negaverint.
